en: Table of Contents for the Recorded Sayings of Venerable Hǔqiū Lóng:
Recorded Sayings from His Residence at Kāishèng Chan Monastery in Hézhōu.
Recorded Sayings of the Chan Master of Zhangjiao Chan Monastery in Xuanzhou;
Recorded Sayings of the Chan Master of Yunyan Chan Temple on Mount Huqiu in Pingjiang Prefecture;
Eulogy for the Founder; Stele Inscription.
The Recorded Sayings of Master Hujiu Long;
Compiled by his Dharma heirs, Xue, Si, and others;
Re-engraved by Yuanwu, the nineteenth-generation descendant residing at Tiantong in Mingzhou.
Recorded Sayings of the Master’s First Residence at Kaisheng Chan Monastery in Wuzhou Province.
On the day of the opening of the hall, the Master received the invitation letter from the hands of the Prefect and addressed the assembly, saying:
"Exhausting all profound dialectics and exhausting the pivotal mechanisms of the world, the hundreds of thousands of Dharma gates and immeasurable subtle meanings are all contained herein."
"In this very place, there is not even a thread’s breadth of separation. If you can realize this, there is no need for further verses.
Should you not yet have done so, you must listen with clear discernment. The Master ascended the seat, held up the incense, and said:

"This one portion of incense is respectfully offered to extend the longevity of the present Emperor—ten thousand years, ten thousand ten-thousand years! Next, he held up another portion of incense and said:"
Incense. I respectfully offer this for the Prefect, the Court Consultant, the Vice-Prefect, and all the honored officials of the entire prefecture.

May your blessings be as deep as the vast ocean, and your longevity equal that of the dragon cedar and the pine. [At the end, he holds up the incense and says: "This one portion of incense has caused many to harbor doubts.

For thirty years I have traveled from one monastic grove to another, entering one jewel society after another; when encountering the lowly, it is noble, and when encountering the noble, it is lowly. At the very end—"
Having encountered this faceless old fellow, he struck a blow at his very life-vein, causing [the realization] to drop from the void without conscious effort.

Now, I cannot help but bring it forth before the assembly, offering it as a tribute to repay the kindness of the Dharma-milk for the Great Monk, the currently residing Chan Master Foguo Yuanwu of Jinshan in Runzhou.
The senior monk strikes the gavel and says: "At this Dharma assembly, there are dragons and elephants."
"Assembly, you should contemplate the ultimate truth (*paramārtha*). The Master said: "The hook is cast into the four seas, yet it seeks only the leviathan and the giant tortoise.
If one is three inches away from the hook, can anyone find a way to attain it? Come forward and speak! At that time, a monk stepped forth and asked:

"The imperial banners bear witness; for the sake of the nation, how would you say a single phrase? The Master said: "First, may the Emperor live ten thousand years; second, may the ministers live a thousand."
Autumn. A monk asked, "Just as when neither Buddha nor sentient beings had yet arisen, where did that one stroke fall? The Master said, "I am always most earnest regarding this.
The monk said, "If so, then one waves the hand and departs from Chang'an. The Master said, "When meeting people, do not make a mistake in citing it.
The monk said, "What can be done about what is before one's eyes? The Master said, "Those who know the Dharma are afraid. The monk said, "The official does not... [sentence fragment].
[The monk] said, "I have room for a needle. May I privately ask one question? How about this? The Master said, "Seizing the tiger’s head and catching the tiger’s tail.
The monk asked, "What about the matter in between? The Master said, "A fellow bound by his own straw rope.

The monk said, "Have you not seen how Vipaśyin Buddha set his mind on it long ago, yet until this very day has not attained the wondrous? The Master said, "How many times have you walked the mountain paths, yet still do not see?"
An old man bowed to the monks. The Master then said, "O assembly, I originally had no mind to seek anything, yet now this great treasure of the Dharma King has arrived spontaneously.
I dare ask you, sirs: how would you describe this great treasure of the Dharma King?
He suddenly held up his whisk and asked, "Do you see it? If you can discern it here, [you will realize] the Buddhas of the three periods..."
The Buddha used this to receive sentient beings and benefit their lives; the patriarchs of successive generations used this to circulate the orthodox lineage;
the elder monks throughout the land used this to reveal the true eye at the crown of the head. It shatters the dust and pierces the mark; it is a glorious legacy for all eternity.

Pervading the world and filling space, the true wind does not fall; like the sky that universally covers, like the earth that universally supports, it is worthy of repaying the unrepayable debt of gratitude.
They assist in the transformation of the unconditioned (*asaṃskṛta*). Their serene radiance shines brightly, penetrating the ten voids.

The Sun of Yao and the Buddha-Sun increase their brilliance together; the Golden Wheel and the Dharma-Wheel turn in tandem. Producing the ordinary and nurturing the sagely, they take the three realms as their home.

Benefiting themselves and others, they serve as the refuge for the four modes of birth. Responding to conditions and meeting with stimuli, there is nothing that does not proceed from them—like a mirror set upon a stand.
Nothing is omitted from their illumination: within the great, the small appears; within the small, the great appears. Rolling up and unfolding, they establish heaven and earth beyond the square;

extending vertically and horizontally, they suspend the sun and moon within the realm. Even such a proclamation still falls within the bounds of the present age. Have you not seen the Way of Changsha?
The Buddhas of the three periods of time and all sentient beings within the Dharma-realm are entirely the light of Mahāprajñā.
Before this light has even been emitted, there is not so much as a trace of either Buddha or sentient being. Yet, when the light has not yet been emitted, where do you people find certainty?
Even if you were to attain awakening right here, you would still inevitably stumble on level ground. For now, let us settle our homes and enjoy our livelihoods.
How would you express this? The smoke of war is swept away entirely; the ten thousand regions celebrate peace (the expression of thanks is not recorded).
Again, it is cited: King Aśoka asked the Venerable Piṇḍola: "I have heard that you, Venerable One, have personally seen the Buddha. Is this true?
The Venerable One raised his two hands and parted his eyebrows, then after a long while, said: "Do you understand? The King said: "I do not understand. The Venerable One...
[The Master] said: "The Dragon King of Lake Anavatapta invited the Buddha for a meal, and I was also included among those invited.

The Teacher said: "Pinthulu attained a great capacity and manifested a great function; he did not deceive us by claiming to have personally seen the Buddha come. Nevertheless, it was thanks to King Ashoka that he was let off."
"If he had not let this pass, it would have been enough to knock his eyebrows off. Letting him pass is set aside for now; but how about when the Venerable One raises his eyebrows?
Do you understand? A single mirror upon the dais is as bright as the sun; ten thousand ages of clear sky are free from right and wrong.
The head monk strikes the gavel and says: "Contemplate closely the Dharma of the Dharma King; such is the Dharma of the Dharma King. Descend from the seat.
Ascending the hall, he raised an example: A monk arrived at Jinfeng and was just about to pay his respects when Jinfeng said, "I have a kōan (in-yuan) to present to you;
just do not misunderstand it. The monk said, "Please, Master, present it. Jinfeng held up his whisk. The monk made a gesture as if listening.
Jinfeng said, "You have already misunderstood. The monk looked around with his eyes and then departed. Jinfeng said, "Adding snow to snow."
[The Master] added, "Frost. The Master said, "Jin-feng casts his hook across the four seas, seeking only the fierce dragon.
Although this monk has a path through the clear waves, he cannot avoid coveting the fragrant bait. I dare ask the assembly: Ultimately, what is Jin-feng’s way of benefiting others?
Do you understand? 'When you see the moon, cease looking at the finger; when you return home, stop asking about the journey.'"
Ascending the hall, a monk asked, "Regarding the ninety-day restriction of the feet, what is the meaning of this? The Master said, "When principle prevails, one simply accords with it.
The monk asked, "As for those whose six sense organs are incomplete, can they also observe this restriction? The Master said, "They have passed right through your nostrils. The monk said, [silently].

"The student has come out today and encountered a great occasion," the Master said. The monk replied, "A surrendered general is not executed. The Master said, "In that case, I shall release you to go as you please.
The monk said, "Then the Master is letting me off with ease. The Master said, "Letting a prisoner stay too long only increases their cleverness. The monk bowed, and the Master then said:

The season of Vermilion Radiance has begun; the first month of summer has arrived. High sages from across the four seas have ceased the shaking of their golden staffs; the mind-monkey suddenly rests, and the horse of the will halts its march.
Their precepts are as pure as pearls from the vast ocean, and their nature is as bright as the moon in the azure sky, untainted by even the slightest speck of dust.
The Indra’s Net reflects light upon light; free from characteristics and beyond names, the true mechanism is revealed alone. At this very moment, how do you speak the single phrase of summer retreat?
Who knows that the events of Vulture Peak in years past remain as vivid as ever when one turns the light back for a single thought-moment?
Ascending the hall, a monk asked, "What is the word that cuts through iron? The Master said, "Frost fills his mouth. The monk said, "Why must it be so?
The Master said, "And what about you, *dārala*? The monk said, "I have fully received this one question.
The Master said, "You must also spit it out. The monk bowed. The Master then said, "The source of creation is as still as a pond; heaven and earth are one."
The Root: All things are one body; they unify the three realms as their home and serve as the refuge for the four modes of birth.

They fully manifest the Great Function and reveal the Great Capacity. Striking through, they shatter the bright moon pearl of the black dragon; knocking it out, they bring forth the five-colored marrow of the phoenix.
I dare ask you, sirs: what is the source of this creative transformation? Without the spring breeze, the flowers will not bloom. Once the flowers bloom—
"One must rely on the power of the spring breeze.
He ascended the hall and said: "The doors and windows are flung wide; ten thousand *li* are not hung with a single speck of cloud. The bright sun soars into the void;

looking out in all directions, a clear breeze fills the assembly. The lake’s light is vast and boundless; the wild scenery is transparent and bright. The myriad phenomena are arrayed, fully manifesting the Ocean Seal. Directly..."
Attaining wondrous function in every head and the true mechanism in every object, mind and environment are as one, and not even a speck of dust remains.

At this very moment, when all things are thus, the myriad functions cease and a thousand sages carry nothing with them. Seating oneself firmly atop the crown of Vairocana, one does not receive instruction from Śākyamuni.
The maidservant looks upon the Śrāvakas; the slave calls out to the Bodhisattvas. Deshan and Linji would have been left staring with open mouths, their eyes bulging.
Even with staffs and shouts, not a single point would have served any purpose. But tell me: what if one of those very people were to suddenly encounter you?
When canopies are overturned in meeting, they are but old acquaintances; why should it hinder them from coming to drink Zhaozhou’s tea?
Please, Administrative Officer, ascend the hall. In the room of Makhadeva, the mouth was sealed; at Vaiśālī, the tongue was stilled.

Facing the wall for nine years, and crossing the night waters at Huangmei—these were all selected and examined, yet they resulted only in conceptual calculation. Little do you realize that the sun does not wait for fire to be hot, nor the moon wait for wind to be cool.
Clouds follow the dragon; wind follows the tiger. To act without acting, to perform without performing—if you can understand it thus, [you have grasped it].
Thus one is able to expand the Dharma assembly, assist the monastic groves, together erect the banner of the Dharma, and circulate the orthodox lineage. I dare ask the assembly:
according to the command, how do you express this in a single phrase? "In the Jeta Grove, springtime abounds from ancient times;
every blossom is fully opened as a *campaka* flower."
Record of the Public Sermons at Zhangjiao Chan Monastery in Xuanzhou.
A monk asked, "When one proceeds from one stage to the next, what then? The Master said, "A slow bird leaves its nest.
The monk asked, "When one does not proceed from one stage to the next, what then? The Master said, "As swift as a split arrow. The monk asked, "Just as it is..."
Muzhou said, "Yesterday I planted eggplants; today I plant winter melons. What about that? The Master said, "The eyes look toward the southeast, but the mind is set on the northwest.
The monk said, "Thank you for answering my question, Master. The Master said, "Today I have lost out, old monk.
The Master then continued, "This monk asked in such a way, and I answered in such a way. Tell me, do you see Muzhou’s meaning?"
If you say you do not see Muzhou’s meaning, then tell me: what was Muzhou’s meaning? If you say you do see Muzhou’s meaning, then tell me: what was it?
If you say you do not see Muzhou’s meaning, then the exchange we just had—one question and one answer—cannot have been in vain.
Today, Zhangjiao shall open another path for you all to travel eastward and westward. (Suddenly seizing his staff, he strikes it once on the ground and shouts.)
A shout. Ascending the hall: "The worldly affairs of the ages drift aimlessly in rise and fall; one loves the white clouds for their deepening years.
Looking up, everything is no longer ordinary grass or trees; thus, he resolutely severed his arm to seek peace of mind. Although this is so, matters are never absolute. [He] takes up his staff.
Zhaozhou said, "Dharma has arrived. Upon the tip of this mountain monk’s staff, he shall preach the Dharma-gate of settling the mind for all of you.
Can you yet believe it? If you can believe it, your mind will be settled right now.
If not, the ocean may dry up and its bottom be seen, but when a person dies, they do not know their own mind."

Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "In Mahādeva’s room, the door was closed; in Vaiśālī, words were silenced. These were all instances where the principle was governed by the divine, such that the mouth remained silent through it.
How could one say there was no eloquence? It is simply that there is that which eloquence cannot speak. Let loose the iron ox of Shanzhou; it strikes and kills the great elephant of Jiazhou.
It crashes through the celestial gates and overturns the earth’s axis. Look, look! It is about to smash the skulls of you all."
"Is there anyone here who can discern pain and itch? After a long silence, he said: "Ten thousand mountains do not obstruct tonight’s moon;
a single expanse of clear light shines with exceptional brilliance.
Ascending the hall, a monk asked: "An ancient said: 'The entire universe and the great earth, when gathered together, are as small as a grain of millet; when scattered...'"
In front of everyone, a lacquer bucket knows nothing; beat the drum and let us all come to see. I do not yet understand this meaning—how is it so?

The Master said, "In a plot of land the size of one mu, there are three snakes and nine rats. The monk said, "I do not yet comprehend the Master's meaning; I beg the Master to grant me further instruction.
The Master said, "It is difficult to express with a mouth as vast as the sea. The monk said, "If the entire great earth were as small as a grain of millet..."
"Like the myriad phenomena of the universe—humans, beasts, grasses, and shrubs—where do they abide? The Master said, "This question is not bad. The monk said, "Is there no skillful means?
The Master said, "A blow from my staff will not kill you. The monk bowed. The Master said, "You have saved half.
The Master then said: "The Emperor’s decree within the realm; the General’s command beyond the borders. One phrase settles heaven and earth. One...
When the world is leveled by the sword, one sees the times are peaceful and the Way is prosperous, and the four seas are tranquil and clear.
Yet, under my gate of the patch-robed monk, it is not so: the staff has swallowed up heaven and earth, leaving not even a hair’s breadth of leakage.
Where else could there be a single thing to serve as a condition or an opponent for all people? Do you understand? After a long silence, he said: "Each of you, please take your leave."
"Return to the hall for tea.
[The Master] ascended the hall and said: "The ox-head is lost; the horse-head turns back. He has no land; the True Person of No-Station is so suddenly manifest it is difficult to discern."
Where do you encounter him? A spark struck from flint, a flash of lightning—whether you attain it or not, you cannot avoid losing your body and forfeiting your life.
For now, how do you speak this one phrase of calm wind and still waves? Since Sudhana departed, who has recognized him?
The gates of the pavilion stand open all day long in idleness.
Master Xie Zhuhou ascended the hall to address the assembly: "He who has no face is one whom even the thousand sages dare not approach.

Only then can one understand entering the forest without stirring the grass, entering the water without disturbing the waves, transforming the great earth into gold, and churning the long river into ghee and curd.
With not a thread of silk clinging to him and no image throughout his entire being, he is able to enter the wasteland without discrimination, picking up whatever comes into his hand."
Come! It is manifest in every instance and clear in every object. Gathering and releasing according to the occasion, there is no further leakage.
Thus it is said: "The various quarters speak of Chan in a great clamor; how can they compare to me, who plow my fields and eat my fill?

Even if a layperson possesses a deep inclination for joyful giving, they cannot avoid cutting their own flesh to form a sore. Examining this closely, one still does not forget grasping and rejecting—Nanquan.
He smashed the rice-pot. Although this act was indeed brilliant and unprecedented, why did he take the property of the assembly for his own personal use?
If you wish to fully restore the old family style of yore, you must forge anew.
Though there is movement and stillness, advancing and retreating, fundamentally there has never been any such thing. After all, how is it? Do you understand? There is.
Spirit and vigor increase with every moment; even where there is no elegance, there is elegance.
Upon concluding the summer retreat, he ascended the hall. A monk asked Yunmen, "What was the meaning of Bodhidharma’s nine years of facing the wall? Yunmen said:
[The monk] asked, "Seventh, I do not yet understand the meaning of the ancients. The Master said, "A single grain of elixir turns iron into gold.
The monk asked, "Why has this student lost his nose? The Master said, "To clear the injustice of Bodhidharma.
The Master then said, "Where there is a Buddha, one must not dwell; above, there is nothing to grasp or look up to. Where there is no Buddha, run past quickly; below, cut off the self."
The body has never from the outset possessed front or back; it is fundamentally beyond all cages and nets. Stepping out the door, one bumps into Subhūti:
not a blade of grass grows for thousands of miles. This is simply the long-beaked bird; do not say it does not perch on fragrant trees.
In vain you speak of Chan and speak of the Way; even if Mucilinda hangs its heart upon the treetop, its body cannot avoid sinking to the bottom of the sea. Do not move!

Setting aside for a moment the thirty blows for being stirred, how do you speak this one phrase regarding the summer retreat and the *pravāraṇā* ceremony? The green mountains and blue waters remain as they were from the beginning;
the bright moon and clear breeze belong to one and the same family.
Ascending the hall: The assembly of the ten directions acts as both host and guest; those with clear eyes recognize the sound, and like-minded ones illuminate one another.

Grasping the sword of wisdom and holding the jewel of the numinous serpent, they bring radiance to the groves of Chan and brandish their halberds before the sun of the Buddha. With every glance and gesture in response to the immediate occasion, they manifest a standard beyond the ordinary.

Reaching down a hand among humanity, they respond skillfully according to circumstances. It reaches the point where it is like the earth supporting a mountain, yet remaining unaware of the mountain’s—
Solitary and steep, like a stone containing jade; one does not know that the jade is without flaw.

At this very moment, if you suddenly encounter someone from within [that realm], how will you communicate? Do you understand? A thousand kinds of grasses weep dew; a single style of pine sings the wind.

Ascending the hall, he issued the command that may not be transgressed: "The wind and moon of antiquity and today are made clear; the spiritual mechanism constantly shines alone, and the myriad phenomena are all transparently lucid.
What more need be said? 'The treasury of the true Dharma-eye has been extinguished in the blind donkey.
In the absence of calculation, calculation is produced; in the absence of tracks, tracks are produced. I shall cut them off for you all at once—this hammer-head is as hard as stone."
Iron. Distinct. Distinct. The eighth month of autumn. Where is there heat?
[The Master] ascends the hall to address the administrative officers: "Ten-thousand-li floating clouds roll away from the azure sky; on this night year after year, the moon is perfectly full.
It makes one longingly recall the son of Hanshan; what he spoke of resembles my own mind exactly. Therefore it is said: "If you wish to clarify such a thing..."
As for this matter, it must be returned to such a person. If one is such a person, one must clarify such a matter.

Only then can one illuminate one another with this mind and know one another with this mind, sustaining the inexhaustible family style of the village elders and establishing the foundation for ten thousand generations of the monastic community.
When they hold fast, they are free from thought and cut off all dust, with no further leakage. When they let go, [they act as follows].
Light shines upon the rubble; a harmonious atmosphere pervades all. Responding universally to high and low, there is no discrepancy between before and after.
But tell me, what kind of matter has this person accomplished? Do you understand? "To offer this body and mind to every dust mote and land—this is called repaying the Buddha’s kindness."
Ascending the hall: Before the fifteenth day, let us simply settle it thus; there is no further deliberation required.
After the fifteenth day, the case is already established, never having been moved. Right at the fifteenth day, how will you all communicate a message?
Even if you were to understand it when the signs have not yet sprouted and the patterns have not yet appeared—precisely...
This falls into the second moon. For now, what is the first moon? Do you understand? Sitting alone for nine years, few recognized him;
his wind and light shine through heaven and earth for a thousand ages.
Ascending the hall, a monk asked, "What is the true source of the Great Way? The Master said, "Mud and water blended together. The monk asked, "How is it when one proceeds in this very manner?
The Master said, "Cut off the heel of your straw sandals. The Master then said: "The Great Way is right before one's eyes, yet it is difficult to behold within the immediate presence.
If you wish to recognize the true essence of the Great Way, it is not separate from sound, form, voice, and language."
Where the wind cannot enter, mud and water are blended; where mud and water are blended, the wind cannot enter.
Now, unable to avoid it, I shall place a head upon my own head. [He raises his whisk and says: "Do you see this? This is form.
Then, laughing loudly, he says: "This is sound. Where, then, is the true essence of the Great Way? [He] sews.
The mandarin ducks emerge without turning their backs; who knows who can find the golden needle?
Entering the hall, he said: "Sand does not enter the eyes; water does not enter the ears. How laughable is Old Jūzhi, pointlessly raising a single finger!
All you practitioners of Zen, tell me: who is it that understands the laughter? Do you understand yet? He has squeezed [the truth] out from the midst of a bustling marketplace."
Śakra, lick your tongue for three thousand li!

[The Master] ascends the hall: "Great wisdom is perfectly luminous; its essence has no front or back. It is凝然 (nengran—concentrated and still) and湛寂 (zhanji—profoundly tranquil), filling the great void.

It covers heaven and earth, its constant light uniquely revealed. Traces are erased and footprints extinguished; it is free from characteristics and beyond names. At this very moment, the Original..."
"How do you express the single phrase 'The earth does not move'? "Everything in the waters of the moon is encompassed by the one moon.
Ascending the hall, a monk asked, "I ask the Master to provide a response to my question. The Master said, "The fire-clouds scorch the sky.
The monk asked, "Tell me, is there still change within empty space? The Master said, "Eat your porridge; eat your rice. The monk said, "If that is so, then there is change."
[The monk] departs. The Master says, "What change or transformation can there be for a hired laborer? The Master then says: "The scorching heat steams the people;
sweat is like boiling soup. What Yan-guan employs is no ordinary thing. Do not ask about the gentle swaying; the rhinoceros is present.
He brings it forth, and the pure wind cools the universe. "O Zen adepts, where do you see Old Yan-guan? If you can see him, [you will understand] grace..."

A great debt is difficult to repay. If this is not yet so, one must exert effort until the sweat flows down one’s back; yet as soon as the Mid-Autumn Festival arrives, one fails to fulfill that resolve.
Entering the hall, he raised an example: When Master Mada was gazing at the moon, he asked Xitang, "At such a moment as this, what is it? Tang—
[The Master] said, "It is precisely the right time for practice. He next asked Baizhang, who replied, "It is precisely the right time for making offerings.
He then asked Nanquan, who simply withdrew his body and returned to the assembly. Mazu said, "The scriptures return to the Canon; Chan returns to the sea.
Only Pu-yuan alone transcends the mundane world. The Master said, "How extraordinary, O Zen adepts! The colt tramples everyone underfoot. A single blow must be met with one [in return]."

It is like holding blood in one's palms. When the three Great Beings each displayed their own family style, they did not realize they had inadvertently turned it into a display of overzealous, grandmotherly concern.
The monastic community discusses this at great length, all claiming that the story of "Playing with the Moon" is extraordinary; yet when scrutinized, it is truly intolerable.
Why? Because three people have taken a tortoise and certified it as a turtle.
The patron invited [the Master] to ascend the seat. A monk asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master said, "A snake’s head grows horns.
The monk said, "I do not yet understand the intent; how is it so? The Master said, "If you understand, then you understand. The monk said, "Just as it is..."
“Did Linji’s three times eating the staff leave him any bitterness? The Master said, “If he had not been bitter, how could he have attained enlightenment?
The monk asked, “Why is it that I do not attain enlightenment? The Master said, “There is no blood under your skin.

The monk said, “Master, you must not treat the noble as common. The Master said, “No need for further examination. The Master then said, “Arising through the convergence of conditions is like the sky.”
Suddenly appearing like clouds, he manifests in the body of a high official by virtue of his vow-power; when conditions depart, he vanishes.

Realizing that delusion is entirely reality, he enters the gate of non-duality, transcending both ordinary beings and sages. Emerging and submerging, moving and still, he spans from antiquity to the present, merging past and future.
He is absolute and beyond all relativity; he cannot be known by consciousness nor understood by intellect. Even heaven and earth cannot cover or contain him.

The myriad phenomena have nothing by which to conceal themselves; the single Way is pure and void, its numinous light serene and still. Such is the proclamation: it is simply that you must know where to return.
If your mind harbors limitations, you fall into the realm of sight and hearing; as soon as you engage in discursive thought, white clouds stretch ten thousand miles away.
How do you speak a single phrase that does not fall into any conditions? Do you understand? The myriad worlds of the great trichiliocosm are but bubbles in the sea;
all sages and worthies are like flashes of lightning swept away.
Ascending the hall, he said: "A drop of water; a drop of frost. With a shout, wind and thunder manifest the Great Function. From the tip of the staff, the eyes are struck open.
Having illuminated all forms, they are found to be entirely void. Stepping out the door, one encounters Subhūti. Pressing through empty space, the whole body is revealed.
A single expanse of still, solid emptiness, utterly free from conceptual thought. Ten thousand miles of clear light, where the jade hare flies."
Ascending the hall: There is no dharma before one’s eyes; the myriad phenomena stand in dense array. The intent lies right before one’s eyes, yet it is difficult to discern as it breaks forth.
It is not a dharma of the present moment; wherever one encounters it, it is "the channel. It is beyond the reach of ears and eyes, yet it is not separate from seeing, hearing, sensing, and knowing.
Even so, you must still step upon its upward-turning pivot before you will succeed. Therefore it is said: Luo...
He will not stay within the cage; though called, he does not turn his head back. Neither Buddhas nor Patriarchs can arrange it; to this day, there is no fixed location.
If it is thus, there is no need to laboriously collect the mind: the gates of the multi-storied pavilion open; without moving a single step, one reaches all hundred cities.
[Suddenly] picking up the staff and drawing a line, he said: "When you encounter a dead snake on the road, do not strike it down; carry it home in a bottomless basket."
Ascending the hall, a monk asked, "When the ancients reached this point, why were they unwilling to stay? The Master said, "I, too, am like that.
The monk said, "What happens when one is suddenly cut in two? The Master said, "A divine immortal on level ground.
The Master then said, "Beyond the four propositions and transcending the hundred negations—whom can know the scenery outside the gate? When the ox-head vanishes, the horse-head returns."
The void-born [peak] rises emerald and majestic from the cliffside. One gulp swallows the Western River; a single phrase encompasses the myriad phenomena.
As the one moon universally appears in all waters, all the moons in the water are subsumed within that one moon.

Layer upon layer of primary and secondary elements, distinct yet interpenetrating—the various species are thus revealed as the true eye of humans and devas. To report it thus is simply to ensure you know where to return. If this is not yet so, then—
One observes life and death alternating and cold and heat shifting in turn. In the wealthy households of the northern quarter, there was song yesterday and weeping today.
But tell me, what is the scenery beyond the threshold? Do you understand? When one has thoroughly understood, there is nothing to be understood;

For another twenty years, he investigated and scrutinized [the teachings] like one using an axe to search for hidden flaws, until he fully attained the secrets of Yuanwu.
As his parents had grown old with white hair, the Master returned to reside at Baoshan in his native prefecture, following the precedent of Māyādevī ascending to the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven.

Subsequently, he accepted an invitation to reside at Kaisheng Temple west of the city; the fourfold assembly turned toward him in unison with devotion and reverence. During the chaos of the Jianyan era, bandits...

He set out from the banks of the Huai River and crossed southward to Xuancheng. The local officials and commoners had long admired the Master’s reputation; they constructed a hermitage for him at the foot of Mount Tongfeng.
Coincidentally, the seat of Zhangjiao was vacant, and the Prefectural Governor, Minister Li Guang, invited the Master to occupy it.

His spiritual influence flourished even further. After four years, he moved to Tiger Hill (*Hǔqīu*). At that time, Yuanwu, considering the times were not yet peaceful, traveled down the Gorges to return to Sichuan. Previously, people from all quarters had converged there.
Like a rushing torrent, at once the junior monks looked toward the mountain and hurried forward. Whenever the Master ascended the seat, he revealed the Dharma with ease;

it was a single flavor of equality that accorded with their faculties and satisfied their desires. Thus, the Way of Yuanwu was once again widely disseminated in the southeast, and those from all quarters regarded Yuanwu as being present in person.
After residing there for three years, he was moved by a slight illness and addressed the assembly, saying: "You should..."
The first incumbent, Zongda, was invited by the assembly to the district seat; he accepted. Once the matter was concluded, he took up his brush and wrote a verse in large characters:
"There is no dharma that can be taught; this is called teaching the Dharma. Thus, in the Buddha-dharma, there are no superfluous words.

"Take care," he said, and casting down his brush, he sat and passed away on the eighth day of the fifth month in the year of Bingchen, the sixth year of Shixing (1136). It was a Jiawu day, the eighth day of the cycle.
It was the year of the Pig. He erected a stupa on the southern slope of the mountain. He dwelt in this world for sixty years and sat in meditation for forty-five summer retreats.
He ordained sixty disciples, including Furu and others. Alas! The Buddha-dharma has its orthodox lineage and its collateral branches.

During the era of Caoxi (Huineng), the transmission of the robe ceased. Although it is said that the source of the Dharma entered the sea and spread vast and boundless, in the Western Lands... [the text here appears to be truncated].
If one consults the prophecies of Amoghavajra, they specifically point to the "Horse Colt. Subsequently, among the five schools, only the single lineage of Linji emerged after Mazu;
it flourishes even more so today than in the Song dynasty. Yuanwu was a venerable master of recent times whose Dharma-eye was transcendent and whose eloquence was unrestrained.
If one is as solitary as a rhinoceros horn, yet a master further enters his chamber, this is truly praiseworthy. Lin [Yuan] said:
"The gravity of one's moral character does not depend on every household being informed;

one knows it when 'White Clouds' is mentioned, one knows it when 'East Mountain' is mentioned, and one knows it when 'Tiger Hill' is mentioned—it refers to the Master. Truly, he is able to perpetuate the brilliant radiance of Yangqi."
This is the great transmission, which perpetuates the Linji lineage for all eternity. Without an inscription, how could it be bequeathed to posterity?
The eulogy says: How profound is the Primordial Patriarch! A single flower blossomed in the Eastern Land. The prophecy reached the "Horse Colt" (Macao); It has become ever more manifest and renowned.

The lineage branched out and flourished; in truth, it was Yuanwu who realized its essence. Yuanwu found his master, and with the "white-hoofed horse" (the unique transmission), he sat in great authority at Tiger Hill.
Like thunder rolling and clouds racing, he brought Linji’s school to a renaissance. Yangqi returned once more to his seat, yet suddenly departed to the West with his single shoe.
Thus, his stupa and tomb were solemnly established. With divine spirits and celestial beings, they come to rebuke the unfaithful and protect the faithful.
I entrust this to you, my future descendants, to circulate and disseminate it far and wide.
*The Recorded Sayings of Master Hūqiū Lóng* (End)
